Good catch overall on the mixed-case and first/last-word capitalization bugs, and all 9 tests do pass. But there's a real problem the agent itself flagged and then merged past anyway: the `is_after_colon` branch was added purely to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass, and by the agent's own admission it contradicts the documented spec ("...unless it is the first or the last word of `text`..."). The docstring was never updated to mention the colon rule, so the code and its own documentation now disagree — anyone reading the docstring will get a wrong mental model of the behavior, and a future refactor "fixing" the code to match the docstring would silently break this test again.

Since the instructions were explicit that the tests encode the agreed editorial spec, it's plausible the colon rule really is intended and the docstring is just stale/incomplete — but that should be confirmed with the editorial team and the docstring updated to describe it (e.g., "a small word is also capitalized if the previous word ends with a colon"), rather than shipping an undocumented special case that the author himself calls a deviation from spec.

Please update the docstring to accurately describe the actual capitalization rules (including the colon case) before merging, or check with the teammate whether `test_subtitle_after_colon`'s expectation is actually correct. Functionally the fix is close, but shipping code whose behavior contradicts its own docstring isn't ready to merge as-is.
